items.title: Inflation and retail data dominate the week's economic calendar
points: Wednesday's July Consumer Price Index (CPI — a measure of price changes for a basket of consumer goods and services) is expected to show core inflation easing to 2.5%.
Thursday brings the Producer Price Index (PPI — tracks prices producers receive, an early signal for consumer inflation) and Friday brings retail sales.
The data follows a stronger-than-expected July jobs report and will shape expectations for Federal Reserve rate policy.
One Seeking Alpha contributor argues July CPI could come in 'hot,' potentially accelerating an AI-bubble burst.

items.title: 13F filings reveal institutional positioning
points: Hedge funds and institutional managers must disclose latest holdings this week via 13F reports (quarterly SEC filings showing what large investors own).
Analysts are watching portfolio shifts in Nvidia, Meta, Tesla, CoreWeave, and Corning for changes in institutional conviction.

items.title: Semiconductor and AI earnings on deck
points: Applied Materials reports Thursday, with focus on semiconductor equipment demand and AI-related capital spending.
Super Micro Computer reports Tuesday; CoreWeave reports mid-week; Coherent and other chip suppliers also report.
Other names on the calendar include Cisco, JD.com, and Pershing Square.
AI investors will also track the Needham AI Infrastructure Conference.

items.title: Tech product launches and consumer events
points: Google unveils its latest Pixel smartphones Wednesday as part of its annual hardware refresh.
Amazon's Zoox begins charging fares for robotaxi rides in Las Vegas on Monday, a commercialization milestone for autonomous vehicles.
Netflix streams an MLB game Thursday night and EA launches Madden NFL 27.

items.title: AI agents could power the S&P 500 higher
points: AI agents (software programs that autonomously carry out tasks for people, rather than just answering questions) have spread rapidly across corporate America over the past 18 months.

An Accenture survey found more than two-thirds of C-suite executives say agentic AI delivered greater-than-expected productivity gains, with a similar share of workers reporting higher job satisfaction.
82% of corporate leaders plan to increase AI investments; 78% expect dramatic changes to employee jobs within a year.
Yahoo's executive editor frames the thesis as more agents + more productivity = more profits, supporting higher S&P 500 valuations.

Circle CEO Jeremy Allaire predicts billions of AI agents will eventually perform labor across and between companies, creating agent labor markets; his employees already build personal agent fleets that coordinate via Slack.
Airbnb CEO Brian Chesky says chatbots and coding agents aren't a fix for everything, but the public consistently underestimates AI's actual capabilities.

issues.subject: Morning Brief: How AI agents can power the S&P 500 higher

headlines: AI agents—software programs that can autonomously perform tasks for humans—are rapidly spreading across corporate America and could be a major driver of S&P 500 gains through increased employee productivity and profits.
Two-thirds of C-suite executives report AI agents have delivered greater-than-expected productivity improvements, with 82% planning to increase AI investments.
Circle CEO Jeremy Allaire predicts billions of AI agents will eventually perform work and labor across and between companies, creating new opportunities for entrepreneurs to tap agent labor markets.
78% of corporate leaders expect dramatic changes to employee jobs in the next year due to AI agents, even as job satisfaction improves among workers using the technology.

sections.title: AI Agent Adoption Surging in Corporate America
points: Use of AI agents exploded within companies over the past 18 months, with many CEOs now managing their own teams of agents and requiring employees to learn to build them.

Accenture survey found more than two-thirds of C-suite executives say agentic AI delivered greater-than-expected productivity gains, and roughly the same proportion of workers report higher job satisfaction.

Circle's CEO is aggressively deploying AI agents alongside human workers, with employees building their own agent fleets that can interact through messaging platforms like Slack and coordinate with each other directly.

sections.title: Market Implications and Future Outlook
points: Executive Editor argues the productivity gains from AI agents are helping power higher S&P 500 valuations through the formula: more agents + more productivity = more profits.
82% of corporate leaders plan to increase AI investments, signaling sustained capital deployment into agent technology infrastructure.
Airbnb CEO Brian Chesky noted that while current chatbots and coding agents aren't solutions for everything, the actual capabilities of AI are consistently underestimated by the public.
